# awesome-design-md

Use this skill when the user wants to build a page or product UI that matches an existing public brand system, or when they want a design reference grounded in real-world visual patterns.

This repo is a curated library of DESIGN.md documents that describe:

- visual theme and atmosphere
- color palette and semantic roles
- typography hierarchy
- component styling
- layout principles
- spacing and depth rules
- responsive behavior
- do/don't guardrails

## Best Use Cases

- “Build me a page inspired by Vercel / Stripe / Notion / Linear.”
- “Match this brand aesthetic in a landing page.”
- “Create a high-quality UI that follows this design system.”
- “Review this front-end against a reference design system.”

## Workflow

1. Identify the target brand or product vibe.
2. Choose the closest reference from the awesome-design-md collection.
3. Extract the design rules: palette, type scale, spacing, card treatment, CTA style, density, and layout logic.
4. Translate the extracted system into the current project’s UI.
5. Keep the final implementation consistent with the reference instead of drifting into generic defaults.

## Design Rules to Prioritize

- Preserve the same mood and visual atmosphere.
- Stay faithful to the palette and semantic role of each color.
- Match the typography hierarchy and weight relationships.
- Use compatible spacing and surface treatment.
- Respect the intended content density and responsiveness.
- Keep component shapes, radii, and shadows aligned with the source design.
- Apply the “do/don’t” guardrails to avoid generic AI-looking output.

## Output Standard

When implementing from a DESIGN.md reference:

- keep visual consistency high
- prefer real design logic over decorative filler
- match the underlying system, not just the color palette
- avoid mixing unrelated aesthetic cues from multiple brands

Use the reference as a source of truth for a single coherent brand direction.
